alignments.note: Purpose frame 'so as to' is a rule 7 helper on the infinitive, no conjunction governing the clause. Head on 'gospel' as rule 17's meaning-bearing complement of a support-verb rendering ('bear witness' heads on 'witness'); heading on 'preach' remains defensible.
Supplied intensifier 'even' rides with the preposition it introduces.
Substantival article before an adverb; the supplied nominal is the article's own (rule 22, cf. 'the third part'), headed on the nominal word.
Improper preposition keeps only the English rendering the adverb itself (rule 42).
Supplied clause juncture 'and' is an obligatory English helper on the negated clause the negative introduces (rules 7, 11, 29), not 'added'; taking it as 'added' remains defensible.
Infinitival 'to' is the verb's own helper (rule 7).
Complex prepositional frame rides undivided with the expressed Greek preposition (rule 67, 'eis touto' -> 'in regard of this'), headed on the prepositional word as at 2CO.7.4 and 2CO.7.14.
Substantival article before an adjective supplies the generic nominal itself (rules 22, 49).
'ready to our hand' is the adjective's whole English idiom; 'our' is licensed by it, not 'added' (rule 11).
